nahhas-irab:1-2.t: (حم) (1) (وَالْكِتابِ): genitive (makhfūḍ) by the oath. (الْمُبِينِ) is [part] of its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْناهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُبارَكَةٍ): Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned from the scholars that it is the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr). As for the blessing that is in it, it is the sending down of the Quran. Abū al-ʿĀliya said: it is all mercy; no believing servant who does good happens upon it but his past sins are forgiven him. ʿIkrima said: in it are written the pilgrims, the pilgrims to the House of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, so not one of them is left out and not one is added to them. It was called «مباركة» (blessed) because of the permanence of good in it and its continuance; البركة in the language is permanence and continuance.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: That is, in it is the wisdom from the doing of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: (أَمْراً مِنْ عِنْدِنا): there are five views on its accusative. Saʿīd al-Akhfash said: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense of "commanding" [Translator's note: the source has «أمرين», apparently for «آمرين»]. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: its accusative is the accusative of maṣdars (verbal nouns), that is: "We sent it down a sending down", and the command comprises the reports. Abū ʿUmar al-Jarmī said: it is a ḥāl from an indefinite [noun], and on this basis he permitted «هذا رجل مقبلا» ("this is a man, coming forward"). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «أمرا» is a maṣdar, the meaning being "in it is distinguished a distinguishing", with «أمرا» in the sense of فرق (distinguishing). The fifth view is that the meaning of «يفرق» is "is commanded and carried out", so it becomes like «هو يدعه تركا» ("he leaves it a leaving").

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: (رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ): there are five views on its accusative. Al-Akhfash said: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ construed it as an object, being accusative by «مرسلين», and made the mercy [refer] to the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «رحمة» may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); this is the best that has been said about its accusative. It was also said: it is a badal (substitute) of «أمر». The fifth view is that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). (إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ): «هو» may be redundant (zāʾid), a separating [pronoun] (fāṣil); it may also be a mubtadaʾ (subject) with «السميع» its khabar (predicate), and (الْعَلِيمُ) is [part] of its naʿt (adjective).

nahhas-irab:7-9.t: (رَبِّ السَّماواتِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of «السميع»; it may also be nominative with an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). This is the reading of the Medinans and the Basrans except al-Ḥasan; he and the Kufans read «ربِّ السماوات» [in the genitive; Translator's note: the source's vowelling does not distinguish the two readings] as a badal (substitute), in the sense of "a mercy from your Lord, the Lord of the heavens"; and likewise «ربكم ورب آبائكم الأولين» in the nominative and the genitive.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: [The plural] دواخن has been heard from the Arabs as the plural of دخان (smoke). Al-Qutabī [Ibn Qutayba] claimed that nothing came on this [pattern] except دخان and عثان. Abū Jaʿfar said: This view is worth nothing according to the skilled grammarians; دواخن is only the plural of داخنة. This is the explicit statement of al-Farrāʾ and of everyone whose knowledge is relied on. Al-Farrāʾ reported: دخنت النار فهي داخنة ("the fire smoked, so it is smoking") when it produces smoke.

nahhas-irab:11-12.t: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: that is, the people who were struck by the drought say: «هذا عذاب أليم» ("This is a painful punishment").

nahhas-irab:13-14.t: (أَنَّى لَهُمُ الذِّكْرى): [الذكرى] is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) according to Sībawayh's view, and according to the view of others by an implied verb. Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān said: «أنّى» draws in the meaning of «أين» (where) and «كيف» (how), that is: from which direction and in what state; from it is قالَ يا مَرْيَمُ أَنَّى لَكِ هذا [Āl ʿImrān: 37], that is, from which direction and in what state.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: (إِنَّا): its original is إنّنا, and the nūn was dropped for lightness. (كاشِفُوا الْعَذابِ): the original is كاشفون; the nūn was dropped for lightness. Whoever drops the nūn because of the meeting of two quiescent letters puts العذاب in the accusative. (قَلِيلًا) is accusative because it is a naʿt (adjective) of an adverb (ẓarf) or of a maṣdar (verbal noun). Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: [إنكم عائدون means] "you will return to shirk". It was also said: to the punishment of the Hereafter.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t: (يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ) is accusative in the sense of "remember"; it may not be accusative by «منتقمين», because «إنّ» does not allow the like of this. Abū Jaʿfar and Ṭalḥa read (يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ) [i.e. «نَبْطُشُ», with ḍamma on the ṭāʾ], which is a well-known dialectal form; and the reading of Abū Rajāʾ is (يَوْمَ نَبْطِشُ) [i.e. «نُبْطِشُ»] with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the ṭāʾ, with the object omitted [Translator's note: the source prints all three forms with the same vowelling]. One says بطش and أبطشه. Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā [Thaʿlab] said: (وَجاءَهُمْ رَسُولٌ كَرِيمٌ): that is, [noble] with his Lord, Majestic and Mighty is He; and he said: he said «كريم», [noble] among his people.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: (أَنْ أَدُّوا إِلَيَّ عِبادَ اللَّهِ): «أن» is in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "with [the message] that" (بأن). You put «عباد الله» in the accusative by the action of the verb falling on them, that is: hand over the servants of Allah [to me], that is, release them from the torment. You may also put عباد الله in the accusative as a vocative in construct, the meaning then being: "that you render to me what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has commanded you, O servants of Allah."

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: (وَأَنْ لا تَعْلُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ) is conjoined to the first «أن». (إِنِّي آتِيكُمْ بِسُلْطانٍ مُبِينٍ): Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: that is, with a clear, manifest proof that I am a prophet.

nahhas-irab:20-21.t: (وَإِنِّي عُذْتُ بِرَبِّي وَرَبِّكُمْ): assimilation (idghām) of the dhāl into the tāʾ is permissible because of its closeness to it and because the tāʾ is unvoiced (mahmūsa). (أَنْ تَرْجُمُونِ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, that you revile me. The yāʾ was dropped because it is the head of a verse; and likewise (فَاعْتَزِلُونِ).

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: Whoever says «إنّ هؤلاء» [with kasra], the meaning according to him is: he said, «إنّ هؤلاء».

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: (فَأَسْرِ بِعِبادِي) is from سرى; whoever says أسرى says «فأسْرِ» [Translator's note: the source does not distinguish the two forms here, i.e. «فَاسْرِ» with hamzat al-waṣl versus «فَأَسْرِ»]. (لَيْلًا) is an adverb (ẓarf).

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: (وَاتْرُكِ الْبَحْرَ رَهْواً): [رهوا is accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: one says عيش راه, meaning easy and tranquil; so the meaning of «رهوا» is "still", so that they enter it while it is still and do not flee from it. It was also said: الرهو is that which is parted.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
«كم» in the speech of the Arabs is for multiplicity, and «ربّ» for paucity. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that the origin of «كم» is «كما»: when you say «كم مالك؟» the meaning is "like what thing of number is your wealth?", and the alif was dropped from «ما» just as it is dropped with the genitive particles, as in لِمَ أَذِنْتَ لَهُمْ [al-Tawba: 43]. It was said to him: "Then why did you make the mīm quiescent?" He said: because of frequency of use, as it is made quiescent in poetry; and he recited [metre: al-basīṭ], verse 414:
فلم دفنتم عبيد الله في جدث ... ولم تعجّلتم ولم تروحونا
(So why did you bury ʿUbayd Allāh in a grave, and why did you hasten, and why did you not come to us in the evening?)
Abū al-Ḥasan ibn Kaysān mentioned that this view is unsound, and he argued for that from what the Arabs use in answering «كم», because in answer to «كم مالك؟» they say "thirty" and the like. Had it been as he said, the answer would have been with the kāf, because if someone said «كمن أخوك؟» ("Like whom is your brother?"), you would say «كمحمد» ("like Muḥammad"); and if he said «مثل ما مالك؟» ("Like what is your wealth?"), you would say «مثل الثياب» ("like clothes"); and if he said «كأيّ شيء مالك؟» ("Like what thing is your wealth?"), you would say «كمال زيد» ("like Zayd's wealth"). This is not said with «كم», so it is established that it is not «ما» with the kāf of comparison prefixed to it, and that it is like «من» and «ما», used to ask about number; for if you said «أمالك ثلاثون أم أربعون؟» ("Is your wealth thirty or forty?"), it would not cover the meaning of «كم», because [كم] comprises all of that. It is an indeclinable noun, because it contains the meaning of particles. Sībawayh said: so they are as far from resemblance [to the verb] as «كم» and «إذ» are from the fully declinable [nouns].

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: In [the narration of] Abū Ṣāliḥ from Ibn ʿAbbās: the noble station (al-maqām al-karīm) is the fine dwellings. Abū Jaʿfar said: It is well known in the language that the place where one stays is called «مقام كريم». In [the narration of] al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās: the station is the pulpits; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said the same, and it is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar. We have mentioned it with its chain of transmission in Sūrat «al-Shuʿarāʾ».

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: Yaʿqūb ibn al-Sikkīt said: النَّعمة is enjoyment of ease. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: «فكهين» means "delighted"; and from him: «فاكهين» means "rejoicing". Abū ʿUbayd reported from Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī that one says رجل فكه when he is good-humoured and much given to laughter. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that فكه and فاكه have one meaning, as one says حذر and حاذر. As for Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad], he made a subtle distinction between فَعِل and فاعل in the like of this, saying: الحذر is the one in whose nature is caution, and الحاذر is the one who is on guard (prepared). Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a sound, clear view, and what indicates it is that حذر is intransitive according to the grammarians.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: The kāf [in كذلك] is in the position of the nominative, that is: the matter is that; it may also be in the position of the accusative, in the sense: thus He does with those He destroys and takes vengeance upon.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: (فَما بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ السَّماءُ وَالْأَرْضُ): most exegetes hold that it is literal, and that over the believer weep the place of his prayer on earth and the place of his ascent in heaven. It was also said: it is figurative, the meaning being: neither the people of heaven nor the people of earth wept over them. A third view: it is analogous to the Arabs' saying «ما بكاه شيء» ("nothing wept over him"). «بكت» came [feminine] according to the femininity of السماء; al-Farrāʾ claimed that some Arabs make it masculine.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: [المهين is] a naʿt (adjective) of العذاب. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is (مِنَ الْعَذابِ الْمُهِينِ) [Translator's note: so in the source; from what follows, the reading meant is the genitive construct «من عذاب المهين»], and he took it as the annexation of a thing to itself, like وَذلِكَ دِينُ الْقَيِّمَةِ [al-Bayyina: 5]. Abū Jaʿfar said: The annexation of a thing to itself is impossible according to the Basrans, and the reading contradicts the main body [of the codices]. Were it sound, its implied form would be "from the punishment of the humiliating Pharaoh", then the adjective was put in the place of what it qualifies, and there would be a proof of the omission.

nahhas-irab:31-31.t: It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: he said: [i.e. «من المسرفين»] "of the idolaters"; and from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: he said: "of the murderous".

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: (وَلَقَدِ اخْتَرْناهُمْ): the pronoun refers back to the Children of Israel, that is, We chose them for messengership and honour. (عَلى عِلْمٍ): because whomever We chose among them for messengership would carry out its delivery. (عَلَى الْعالَمِينَ): because of the multitude of messengers among them. It was also said: the world of the people of their time.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: The soundest thing said about it is that البلاء here is blessing, as in «وجميل بلائه لديك» ("and His fine favour towards you"). Al-Farrāʾ said: البلاء here may also be punishment.

nahhas-irab:34-39.t:
(ما خَلَقْناهُما إِلاَّ بِالْحَقِّ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) (39)
(إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ لَيَقُولُونَ إِنْ هِيَ إِلَّا مَوْتَتُنَا الْأُولى): that is, they say this out of habit, without proof, when the evidences had been made clear to them and the proofs had appeared to them. For this reason no argument was made against them here; rather they were made to fear and were threatened, and it was said: (أَهُمْ خَيْرٌ أَمْ قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ), that is, they knew that those were mightier than them. (وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) is conjoined to «قوم»; it may also be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with what follows it as its khabar (predicate); and it may be in the position of the accusative by an implied verb indicated by «أهلكناهم». (إِنَّهُمْ كانُوا مُجْرِمِينَ).

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ permitted (إِنَّ يَوْمَ الْفَصْلِ مِيقاتُهُمْ) with the accusative [i.e. «ميقاتَهم»]. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: then يوم would be accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), the implied form being "that their appointed time is on the Day of Decision". Abū Jaʿfar said: inna and its noun may be separated by an adverb, so you say «إنّ حذاءك زيدا» ("Facing you is Zayd") and «إنّ اليوم القتال» ("Today is the fighting"), because the adverb carries its meaning in the speech even if you do not pronounce it; there is no disagreement among the grammarians about this. They disagreed about the ḥāl (circumstantial): al-Akhfash permitted putting it first, and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] forbade it. Al-Akhfash permitted «إنّ قائمين فيها إخوتك», putting قائمين in the accusative as a ḥāl. «أجمعين» is in the position of the genitive as tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ and mīm.

nahhas-irab:41-42.t: (يَوْمَ لا يُغْنِي مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى شَيْئاً): you put يوم in the accusative as a badal (substitute) of the first يوم. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (مَوْلًى عَنْ مَوْلًى): that is, [a protector] for a friend. (إِلَّا مَنْ رَحِمَ اللَّهُ): there are four ways of parsing «من». Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: «من» is in the position of the nominative as a badal, its implied sense being "and none will be helped except whom Allah has mercy on". It may also be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: "except whom Allah has mercy on, for he will be pardoned". Others said: «من» is in the position of the nominative in the sense "none will avail except whom Allah has mercy on", that is, none will intercede except whom Allah has mercy on. This is a good view, because it is authentically established from the Prophet ﷺ that he will intercede for his community until whoever has in his heart the weight of a mustard seed of faith is brought out of the Fire, and it is authentically established from him that the believers will intercede. The fourth view about «من» is that it is in the position of the accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ); this is the view of al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ.

nahhas-irab:43-44.t: From Abū al-Dardāʾ: he said: «طعام الفاجر» ("the food of the wicked"). This is an exegesis, not a reading, because it contradicts the codex.

nahhas-irab:45-46.t: «كالمهل تغلي في البطون» is the reading of the people of Medina, the people of Kufa and the people of Basra; the reading of Ibn Kathīr is (كَالْمُهْلِ يَغْلِي), and it is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. It contradicts the proof of the community of the people of the cities. The meaning in it is also far-fetched according to Abū ʿUbayd's interpretation, because he made «يغلي» [refer] to المهل, since it is nearer to it; but it is not المهل that boils in the bellies; المهل only boils in cauldrons, as is narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he took silver from the treasury, melted it, then sent for the people of the mosque and said: "This is المهل." And from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: المهل is the dregs of oil. Abū Jaʿfar said: except that dregs of oil can only be said to boil with that [interpretation], according to the apparent sense of the verse [Translator's note: the sentence is obscure in the source and is translated as literally as possible].

nahhas-irab:47-47.t: (خُذُوهُ فَاعْتُلُوهُ) is the reading of the people of Medina, and the people of Kufa read (فَاعْتِلُوهُ) [with kasra on the tāʾ]. They are two dialectal forms, except that analogy requires the kasra, because it is like ضربه يضربه. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh permitted «خذوهو فاعتلوهو», keeping the wāw in continuous speech, except that the preferred choice is to drop it. The grammarians disagreed about that: the position of Sībawayh is that the original is «خذوهو» with the wāw retained, but it was dropped because two letters of prolongation and softness came together; the position of others is that it was dropped because of the two quiescent letters. Juwaybir said, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: it was revealed about Abū Jahl: «خذوه فاعتلوه», when he is ordered [to the Fire] on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: (فَاعْتِلُوهُ) means "push him", (إِلى سَواءِ الْجَحِيمِ), that is, to the middle of Hellfire.

nahhas-irab:48-48.t: It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: الحميم is the hot [water] whose heat has reached its extreme.

nahhas-irab:49-49.t: «إن» has a kasra because it begins [a new sentence]; whoever reads (ذُقْ إِنَّكَ) [i.e. «أَنَّكَ» with fatḥa] takes it in the sense of "because you" or "for that you". The reading with kasra has the proof of the community behind it; moreover, [their] disbelief is greater than his saying "I am the mighty, the noble", because the interpretation of whoever reads it with fatḥa is: "Taste, because you used to say: I am the mighty, the noble."

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: It was said: by this He indicated that they are punished for doubt. It was also said: rather, along with their doubt they denied what they doubted. And whoever doubts something and denies it is disobedient to Allah the Exalted.

nahhas-irab:51-53.t:
[«في مَقام» with fatḥa is] the reading of the Kufans and Abū ʿAmr; the Medinans read (فِي مَقامٍ) [i.e. «مُقام»] with ḍamma on the mīm. Al-Farrāʾ said: مَقام is better in Arabic because it is for the place. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is something for which al-Farrāʾ is reproached: that it be said of readings that the community has transmitted from the community, "this is better than this"; because when the community transmits them from the community, it is said: thus it was revealed, since they do not agree upon error; so how can one of them be better than the other? مُقام with ḍamma has a sound meaning: it may mean "staying" (al-iqāma), as [the poet] said [metre: al-kāmil], verse 415:
عفت الدّيار محلّها فمقامها
(The abodes are effaced, their place of halting and their place of staying.)
مُقام is also the place, if you take it from أقام; and مَقام with fatḥa is also the place, if you take it from قام. (أَمِينٍ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: they are secure in it from hunger, sickness, old age and death, and secure from being expelled from it. Mujāhid said: عَلى سُرُرٍ مُتَقابِلِينَ [al-Ṣāffāt: 44]: none of them sees the back of another's head.

nahhas-irab:54-55.t: (كَذلِكَ): the kāf is in the position of the nominative, that is: the matter is thus; it may also be in the position of the accusative, that is: thus [Allah] does with the God-fearing. (وَزَوَّجْناهُمْ بِحُورٍ عِينٍ): al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الحور are the white ones, and العين those with large eyes. Al-Akhfash said: some Arabs say «بحير عين». Abū Jaʿfar said: this is by making the first follow the second (itbāʿ); its counterpart is [the wording of] whoever narrated «ارجعن مأزورات غير مأجورات» ("Go back burdened with sin, unrewarded"), whereas the clear, eloquent [form] is «ارجعن موزورات» and «بحور». As for «عين», it is the plural of عيناء; it is [on the pattern] فُعْل, whose first radical was given a kasra because a yāʾ follows it.

nahhas-irab:56-56.t: (لا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا الْمَوْتَ إِلَّا الْمَوْتَةَ الْأُولى): [الموتة] is accusative because it is an exception not of the same kind as the first.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t:
(فَضْلًا) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and what governs it is the meaning; there is disagreement about that meaning. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said about it that it is (يَدْعُونَ فِيها بِكُلِّ فاكِهَةٍ آمِنِينَ); he said: what governs it may also be (إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي مَقامٍ أَمِينٍ). Others said: what governs it is (وَوَقاهُمْ عَذابَ الْجَحِيمِ). A fourth answer: all of this governs it, because its meaning, all of it, is a favour from Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.
All of this needs explanation. That is, it may be said: He, Majestic and Mighty is He, has said بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ [al-Anʿām: 127, and Yūsuf: 12 — Translator's note: so cited in the source] and بِما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ [al-Anʿām: 129], so what is the meaning of favour here? There is more than one answer to this. Among them: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, did not impose deeds out of any need of His for them; He imposed that on them only so that they would act and so enter Paradise; so the imposition and their admission into Paradise are a favour from Him, Majestic and Mighty is He. The soundest of the answers in this is that the believers have sins from which they are not free, even if for many of them they are minor; had Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, taken them to account for them, He would have punished them without wronging them; so when He forgave them and admitted them into Paradise, that was a favour from Him, Majestic and Mighty is He. Moreover, Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has blessings upon all His servants in this world; were their deeds set against those blessings, [the blessings] would consume them; so their entry into Paradise has become a favour, as he ﷺ said: «No one enters Paradise by his deeds.» It was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: «Not even I, unless Allah covers me with mercy from Him.»

nahhas-irab:58-58.t: (فَإِنَّما يَسَّرْناهُ بِلِسانِكَ): it was said: the meaning of يسّرناه is "We taught it to you, made you memorise it, and revealed it to you, so that you may be reminded by it and take heed".

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: (فَارْتَقِبْ): that is, wait for Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, to judge between you and them. (إِنَّهُمْ مُرْتَقِبُونَ): there are two views on it. One of them is that it is figurative, the meaning being that they are in the position of those waiting, because the matter will inevitably befall them. It was also said: it is literal, that is, they are waiting for what they hope for.
